key_insight: Kinetic non-equilibrium can leave hypersonic wall-pressure responses nearly unchanged while substantially altering temperature and heat-flux disturbances at higher altitudes.
engineering_relevance: Hypersonic thermal-load and disturbance-response predictions may require kinetic modeling where rarefaction undermines continuum assumptions.
method: Linearize the discrete unified gas-kinetic scheme using complex, time-harmonic perturbations.
Solve the resulting steady elliptic system by pseudo-time marching with LU-SGS acceleration.
Capture shock structure, wall slip, temperature jumps, and non-Fourier heat flux without hybrid coupling.
evidence_signal: Three benchmarks verify the framework; argon blunt-wedge cases at equivalent altitudes of 40 and 50 km show increasing kinetic effects, with significant thermal-response deviations at 50 km despite similar wall-pressure responses.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported benchmarks and argon cases; applicability to reacting air and computational cost are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Kinetic Non-Equilibrium Receptivity Analysis of Hypersonic Flows via a Complex Linearized Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme
